FIRST APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
 ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI)
1.
This Appeal is filed by the owner of the offending vehicle challenging the Judgment and award dated 03.03.2021 passed in MVC No.128/2017 by the learned MACT, Gadag.

2. Brief facts, leading rise to the filing of this appeal are as follows:
On 23.03.2016, the claimant was proceeding towards his agricultural field by riding a TVS XL M/C bearing registration No.KA-26/R-6765.

When he reached near Arashinagodi village, Naragund- Arashinagodi road, at that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/Q-8370 rode the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the claimant's vehicle.
3. As a result of the impact, the claimant fell down and sustained grievous head injuries.
A criminal case was NC: 2026:KHC-D:3647 HC-KAR registered against the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-26/Q-8370.

4. Thereafter, the claimant filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, 'the MV Act') seeking compensation on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.

5. The owner filed the statement of objections admitting the ownership of the vehicle and denying the other averments made in the claim petition, and accordingly, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. Based on the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal, framed the relevant issues.

sentences.text: To substantiate his case, the claimant examined himself as PW-1 and marked eight documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.
The owner did not enter the witness box.

8. The Tribunal, based on the evidence placed on record, partly allowed the claim petition with costs vide judgment dated 03.03.2021 and awarded a compensation of Rs.1,96,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum NC: 2026:KHC-D:3647 HC-KAR from the date of the petition till realization,
directing the owner to deposit the compensation amount.
9. Being aggrieved by the said Judgment and award dated 03.03.2021, the appellant/owner has filed the present appeal.
10. A notice was issued to the respondent/claimant.
Despite service of notice, the respondent/claimant remained unrepresented.

11. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant/owner.
12.
The learned counsel for the appellant/owner contended that the claimant has not examined the doctor to prove the disability and regarding the treatment taken in the hospital.
Without considering the said aspect, the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,96,000/-.
She further submitted that the claimant has not examined the doctor to prove the contents of the discharge summary, and prescription marked as Exs.P6 and P8.

She submitted that the compensation awarded by the tribunal under other NC: 2026:KHC-D:3647 HC-KAR heads is on the higher side, and accordingly,
on these grounds prayed to allow the appeal.

13. Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the owner.
14.
The point that, arises for consideration is with regard to the quantum of compensation.
15. It is an undisputed fact that the claimant met with an accident and sustained grievous injuries.
After the accident, he was admitted to SDM Hospital, Dharwad, where he underwent treatment for 17 days.

16. To prove that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle, the claimant produced the charge sheet marked at Ex.P5, which clearly discloses that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the said motorcycle.
Regarding quantum of compensation:
17. The claimant contended that he was aged about 70 years at the time of the accident and was doing agricultural work, earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Due to NC: 2026:KHC-D:3647 HC-KAR the injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to continue his agricultural work.

18. To substantiate the treatment taken, the petitioner produced the discharge summary marked as Ex.P6, which discloses that he was admitted to SDM Hospital, underwent surgery, and remained as an inpatient for 17 days.

He also produced medical bills marked as Ex.P7, and prescription marked Basappa S/O Mallappa Kolavi vs Basavanttappa S/O Mahadevappa Iti on 7 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139968261/
3 as Ex.P8.
19.

sentences.text: Although the claimant has not examined the doctor, the evidence of PW-1 has not been rebutted by the owner.
20. The Tribunal, after considering the oral and documentary evidence available on record, has awarded compensation of Rs.1,96,000/-, which appears to be just and reasonable.
21. Therefore, I do not find any error or illegality in the impugned Judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
For the foregoing, the point is answered accordingly.

22. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3647 HC-KAR ORDER
The appeal is dismissed.
The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal forthwith.
